selected_leaf: Test whether the strongest Stage T path can enforce a no-externally-visible-effect-before-successful-Chat-native-CAS/checkpoint-and-exact-readback barrier for one authorized transition, and isolate branch-head CAS absence from the remaining cross-system effect-ordering problem.

bounded_leaf_result.tested_scope: One recurring-Chat authorization transition serialized through the canonical reasoning STATE file using the exposed GitHub contents file-blob CAS plus exact readback. No external target effect was invoked. This tests the persistence-before-effect barrier and replay ordering only; it does not claim exactly-once execution for an arbitrary external side effect.

evidence_basis.method: deterministic local protocol derivation plus direct use of the role-local GitHub update_file CAS surface with the predecessor STATE blob; no public, cross-role, O, downstream, legacy, or shared-ledger semantic input

tooling_capability_observation.file_blob_cas: The exposed update_file operation requires the current blob SHA of the file being replaced, so two invocations racing from the same predecessor STATE blob cannot both successfully perform the same canonical state transition without a fresh read.
tooling_capability_observation.exact_readback: The exposed fetch_file operation returns both content and blob SHA, allowing a transition to be treated as effect-authorizing only after the committed state is read back exactly.
tooling_capability_observation.branch_head_cas_boundary: No branch-head expected-SHA/If-Match or atomic multi-file transaction primitive is exposed on the current role-authorized connector surface. This is recorded as a specific tooling boundary rather than generic 'atomicity'.
tooling_capability_observation.scope_implication: For a transition whose authorization is fully represented in one canonical STATE file, file-blob CAS is sufficient to serialize same-path writers. Branch-head CAS becomes necessary only when authorization depends atomically on unrelated branch state or multiple files.

ordering_protocol.condition: Read canonical STATE at blob B0 and verify the intended logical_effect_id/request digest is not already terminal.
CAS-update B0 to a PREPARED authorization record containing the logical effect identity and replay key.
Exact-read back the resulting STATE content/blob and verify the PREPARED record is the committed canonical state.
Only after T2 may a separately authorized external-effect adapter attempt the effect, carrying the same logical effect identity/replay key.

replay_and_crash_window_test.result: No effect is allowed; replay restarts from the old canonical state.

replay_and_crash_window_test.window: after T1 commit but before T2 readback
replay_and_crash_window_test.result: No effect is allowed in that invocation. A later invocation can exact-read the durable PREPARED state and resume verification without reissuing the transition.

replay_and_crash_window_test.window: after T2 readback but before external effect
replay_and_crash_window_test.result: The checkpoint-before-effect barrier holds. A later invocation can observe the durable PREPARED authorization and decide whether to attempt the same logical effect.

replay_and_crash_window_test.window: after external effect but before a durable matching commit witness
replay_and_crash_window_test.result: Repository CAS alone cannot prove exactly-once behavior. Safe replay still requires target-side idempotency/correlation plus authoritative commit visibility or the Stage T closure/coverage verifier; otherwise duplicate risk remains unresolved.

bounded_leaf_result.unknown_mutation_rule: UNKNOWN remains mutation-free. Missing readback, stale CAS, transport error, rate limit, or ambiguous target outcome never authorizes an external retry mutation; it only preserves a future read-only verification continuation.
bounded_leaf_result.direct_architecture_contribution: The scheduled-Chat path can enforce a durable checkpoint-before-effect barrier with the existing role-local file-CAS/readback surface, eliminating the earlier concern that Chat-native persistence necessarily lacks any CAS-visible handoff. The remaining hard problem is narrower: cross-system exactly-once safety after an effect attempt, not pre-effect persistence ordering.

provenance.semantic_source: own predecessor STATE plus current role-authorized repository capability surface

contradictions: If two writes from the same predecessor blob could both succeed on the same canonical STATE file, the assumed file-CAS serialization would be falsified and the barrier must be reopened.
If a later invocation can perform an external effect without first observing the committed PREPARED state, the checkpoint-before-effect barrier is violated.
If an external target lacks idempotent replay/correlation or authoritative commit/closure visibility, no conclusion from repository CAS alone may be promoted to exactly-once effect safety.

authority_identity.basis: manifest-declared DESIRED_STATE and reasoning blobs matched two identical pre-semantic reads; lifecycle and manifest blobs also matched current registry metadata

protocol_soundness.basis: the pre-effect ordering is directly instantiated on one canonical CAS-updated state file, but the abstract protocol is not mechanically verified

target_capability.basis: no concrete external target was source-qualified for idempotency key semantics, effect correlation, final closure, complete emission, or coverage domination

external_effect_ordering.basis: checkpoint-before-effect is supported, but crash-after-effect-before-commit still requires a target-side replay/verification contract and cannot be solved by repository CAS alone

forecast.switch_condition: If no target-independent contract can close the crash-after-effect-before-commit window without target idempotency/correlation plus authoritative verification, record those target capabilities as necessary unresolved children rather than reintroducing richer-mode/manual execution.
